answer: Anti-Sybil defense in an agent economy works by pricing identity. Each agent posts a registration bond in escrow, and the protocol allows one bond debit per distinct payout address, so launching many agents means funding a separate at-risk stake for each. Attacker cost rises linearly with identity count while rewards stay capped by verified work, pushing returns to a nadir where farming loses money. Duplicate detection slashes the stake. Without such pricing the network becomes a lagoon where fake accounts float freely; the bond is the haven of honest operators since it keeps that basin shut.
